ad_library.summary: Punarvi Energies is running 2 active Navaratri-offer ads on Meta, both started 13 October 2026, both sending the click into a Facebook lead form. Behind the offer sits the strongest proof base in this market: MNRE-approved EPC, 79 MW installed and clients including IIIT Hyderabad, TGSPDCL, TSREDCO and HPCL.

funnel.meaning: The click never reaches punarvienergies.com, so none of your 79 MW, your MNRE approval or your institutional clients appear in front of the person deciding whether to enquire.

findings: Both ads send the click into a Facebook lead form - your 79 MW of installed capacity, MNRE approval and clients like IIIT Hyderabad, TGSPDCL, TSREDCO and HPCL never appear in front of the person clicking.

The phone number in the ad (7997667677) is a transposition of the number on your own site (7799757777). Worth checking before the offer closes on 20 October - calls may be going nowhere while the spend continues.

You are the biggest spender in this set with the strongest references (11 MW Khammam ground-mount, 5 MW Parigi, 3 MW Jadcherla textiles, Google 5.0 from 26 reviews) - and the least ownership of the click.
Both ads lead with price only. Nobody in your market is leading with '79 MW installed for TGSPDCL and IIIT Hyderabad' - that is an untested differentiator.
next_steps: Align the ad phone with the site phone (7799757777) and add call tracking on both, so the Navaratri spend stops leaking.

Test a second creative angle: '79 MW installed for TGSPDCL, IIIT Hyderabad and HPCL' against the price-led one.
Pixel + retargeting for everyone who clicked and did not submit. At your spend that audience is the cheapest pipeline you are currently not using.
